html:
SMTO-SCH-0034 — SMTO couldn't start because a machine setup file has a mistake

GUID: f6ec92ef-822c-57ec-8e70-d25fa32eead3
Slug: physical-enrollment-invalid
Domain: SCH · Subsystem: physical

What happened

  • SMTO reads an optional file, set up by an administrator, that says which Gateways run on the same computer. That file has a mistake, so SMTO stopped before starting. Your conversations and tasks were not changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Select Copy error details on the startup screen and send them to the person who installed or manages SMTO. This file is only created and edited by an administrator, and the details show which check failed.
  2. If you or someone else recently changed this file, or re-paired a Gateway, tell the administrator what changed. A Gateway that was re-paired gets a new identity, which no longer matches the one recorded in the file.
  3. Once the file has been corrected, select Start again on the startup screen. SMTO checks the file each time it starts, so it will continue once the file is correct.

What success looks like

  • The startup screen reaches Ready and your conversations appear.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete the data folder or this file to get past the error; removing entries that running work still depends on also stops SMTO from starting.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Bootstrap import of the operator physical-enrollment file (physical-targets.json in the state directory) failed: a duplicate physical target or binding, a target without an authenticated enrollment, a mismatched pinned Gateway TLS identity, or an unsupported file format.

What this means

  • Offline physical-enrollment import finds duplicate physical/enrollment bindings, missing authenticated enrollment, mismatched pinned Gateway proof or an unsupported enrollment-file envelope. Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.

Why this can happen

  • Offline physical-enrollment import finds duplicate physical/enrollment bindings, missing authenticated enrollment, mismatched pinned Gateway proof or an unsupported enrollment-file envelope.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare pinned peer identity and enrollment records, consolidate aliases, and preserve any unresolved live storage claims.

How to fix it

  • Fix physical-targets.json in the SMTO state directory: it must be a version 1 object with a targets list, list each physical_id once with all its aliases and storage evidence combined, give every non-controller target at least one enrollment, and match each gateway_id's tls_spki_sha256 and tls_enrollment to the current pinned Gateway record. Do not remove mappings still used by unresolved resource claims.
  • Check the pinned Gateway identity and consolidate the physical target aliases and storage evidence in the supported offline enrollment configuration.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm current state and correct the reported condition before requesting another attempt. Do not replay work with an unknown outcome.

How to verify the fix

  • Supported offline enrollment validates one coherent mapping without replacing ownership under unresolved work.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained evidence or retry an operation whose effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
